summary: Boonlake is an engine-building Euro from Alexander Pfister where you flip and connect tiles on a personal hex board to automate resource chains over several eras. It's a quieter, more solitaire-feeling game than his other titles, focused on tableau optimization.
criticised: Feels drier and less thematic than Pfister's other designs like Maracaibo or Great Western Trail
Dense iconography and end-game scoring bookkeeping
Low player interaction can make it feel like solitaire at the table

interaction.detail: Each player builds and optimizes their own hex-tile board largely independently, with light competition only over shared tile supply and turn order. Most of the game state lives on individual player boards rather than a shared map.

scoring.why: Points accumulate from tile construction, upgraded buildings, completed goals, and end-game bonuses across multiple eras
scoring.how_you_win: You win by building the most efficient personal engine, converting resources into upgraded buildings and completing scoring goals for the highest total VP.

similar: Merv: The Heart of the Silk Road
